h: Real Fossils Along the Essex Coast
p: Dinosaur fans heading to Clacton are in for a bonus that goes beyond the life-size models. The Essex coast has a seriously interesting fossil story of its own, and it's only a short drive from the pier. At Walton-on-the-Naze, the crumbling cliffs below the Naze Tower are famous among fossil hunters, with ancient sharks' teeth and shells regularly turning up on the beach below.

These fossils are far younger than the dinosaurs, coming from long after the big reptiles disappeared, but for a young collector, finding a genuine shark's tooth on the sand is pure magic. Search the beach rather than the cliff face itself, as the cliffs are unstable and eroding, and always keep an eye on the tide times.

Before a visit, a bit of build-up adds to the fun. Read a dinosaur book together, watch a documentary or let the kids pick a favourite species to look out for. Little ones are often amazed by the sheer size of the bigger dinosaurs, so you might measure out the length of one along the beach afterwards with footsteps to really drive it home.

If your youngest is on the sensitive side, talk about the 4D bit beforehand so the movement and effects don't come as a total shock. Sitting on a grown-up's lap or holding hands can make the difference between a scream of fear and a scream of delight.

After the dinosaurs, Clacton's beaches are perfect for building a sandcastle volcano or digging for your own buried bones. And the rest of the pier, from rides to bowling, is right there whenever the kids are ready for the next adventure.
